assumptions._note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Godrej Industries (GIL), consolidated, Rs crore. History is attributable to GIL shareholders (Screener Net Profit replaced by Profit for EPS, see tools/authoring/GODREJIND.patch.js). The consolidated P&L is built from four blocks that sum to reported revenue and EBITDA: GIL's own chemicals business, Godrej Agrovet (100%), Godrej Properties (100%) and a residual that is mostly Godrej Capital (with hospitality, other businesses, corporate costs and eliminations). Godrej Capital's interest cost and Godrej Properties' large other income sit below EBITDA, so EBITDA margins of the blocks are not comparable with each other. The tax line also carries minority interests. The stock is valued as the street values it: a sum of the parts of GIL's stakes and businesses less holding-company net debt and a holding-company discount. Only the chemicals part uses the forecast; the listed stakes are at 30-Sep-2026 closes.

segments.name: Chemicals (GIL standalone)
segments._why: Oleochemicals (fatty acids ~35% of revenue, fatty alcohols ~21%, glycerine ~10%), surfactants (~22%) and specialty (~11%). FY26 revenue +22% to Rs4,132 cr on volumes +9.4% and higher palm/kernel-oil-linked prices; Q1FY27 revenue +31% (volume +9%, exports +20%). FY27E +15%: Q1 actual, then single-digit growth as the price base rises from Q2. FY28-29E +10%: volume ~8-9% (Kundaim reactor +30% capacity, Valia specialty plant, Kheda ethoxylation, Goa food-additives business, first biosurfactant due in Q2FY27) with flat prices.
segments._marginWhy: Segment EBITDA (PBIT + segment depreciation): FY25 Rs412 cr (12.2%), FY26 Rs361 cr (8.7%) after weak fractionated fatty acid volumes, costlier feedstock and Q4FY26 PBIT of only Rs40 cr. Q1FY27 PBIT Rs159 cr (13.7% PBIT margin) was the best quarter since FY23. The PBIT margin has swung between 8% and 17% (FY20-26). FY27E 11.5% (Q1 strong, rest of year nearer the FY25-26 average); FY28E 11.5%; FY29E 12% as specialty and surfactants rise in the mix.

segments.name: Godrej Agrovet (100%)
segments._why: Animal feed, vegetable oil (oil palm), crop protection (incl. Astec), dairy (Creamline) and foods. FY26 revenue +9%; Q1FY27 +9% (cattle feed volumes ~+15%). 9% a year. GIL owns 65.1%; the 34.9% minority is deducted in the tax line. Consolidated for the P&L only: in the valuation the stake is at its market price.
segments._marginWhy: FY26 EBITDA margin 8.4%, FY25 8.8%, Q1FY27 8.4% (Q1FY26 10.3%) as crop protection revenue fell. 8.3% / 8.6% / 8.8%.

segments.name: Godrej Properties (100%)
segments._why: Real estate revenue is booked when projects are handed over, so it lags bookings by 3-4 years and is lumpy (Q4FY26 Rs3,458 cr, Q1FY27 Rs506 cr). Bookings were Rs34,171 cr in FY26 (+16%) and Rs8,651 cr in Q1FY27 (+22%); deliveries 12.1 mn sq ft in FY26. Revenue FY27E +25%, FY28E +20%, FY29E +15% as the FY23-25 bookings surge is delivered. GIL owns 44.77%; the 55.23% minority is deducted in the tax line.
segments._marginWhy: GPL's own EBITDA is usually negative (FY26 -8.8%, FY25 -1.5%) because overheads and marketing for a Rs34,000 cr booking business are expensed while revenue is recognised years later; most of its profit arrives as other income (interest from joint-venture partners, JV profits; FY26 Rs3,256 cr). -6% / -2% / +2% as deliveries catch up.

segments.name: Godrej Capital and others (residual)
segments._why: Consolidated revenue less chemicals, GAVL and GPL: mostly Godrej Capital (housing finance and MSME/retail loans; AUM Rs27,867 cr at Mar-26, +65%; FY26 total income Rs2,478 cr), plus hospitality, other businesses and eliminations. Residual revenue grew 40% in FY26 and 75% in Q1FY27 (Rs926 cr). FY27E +40%, FY28E +32%, FY29E +28% as AUM growth slows from 65% towards ~30%.
segments._marginWhy: Residual EBITDA was 48% of residual revenue in FY25 and 54% in FY26: for a lender this is profit before interest (Godrej Capital's interest, ~Rs1,356 cr in FY26, is in consolidated interest) and after credit costs, less GIL's unallocated corporate costs. 52%.

assumptions._unallocLabel: Corporate costs not in any block (inside the residual)
assumptions._unallocWhy: Unallocated corporate costs and eliminations are inside the residual block, which is defined so that the four blocks sum to reported consolidated revenue and EBITDA.
assumptions._capexWhy: Consolidated purchase of fixed assets: FY24 Rs1,197 cr, FY25 Rs781 cr, FY26 Rs1,028 cr (chemicals ~Rs135 cr, the rest mainly GAVL and GPL's commercial assets). Rs1,200-1,300 cr a year.
assumptions._depWhy: FY26 depreciation Rs501 cr = 5.1% of average gross block (Rs9,776 cr); Q1FY27 Rs133 cr (Rs532 cr annualised). 5.2% gives ~Rs560 cr in FY27E.
assumptions._treasuryWhy: Net-debt group (borrowings Rs51,564 cr at Mar-26, most of it Godrej Capital's lending book and GPL's project debt); other income is entered separately.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Screener other income includes the share of profit of associates (mainly 23.7% of Godrej Consumer, Rs445 cr in FY26) and exceptional items: FY25 Rs2,636 cr, FY26 Rs4,123 cr, Q1FY27 Rs1,036 cr (Q1FY26 Rs1,352 cr). Most of it is Godrej Properties' interest income from JV partners and JV profits (GPL other income FY26 Rs3,256 cr, Q1FY27 Rs839 cr). FY27E Rs4,000 cr (Q1 run-rate), then +10% a year with GCPL and GPL.
assumptions._interestLabel: Interest (incl. Godrej Capital's cost of funds)
assumptions._interestWhy: FY26 Rs2,470 cr, of which ~Rs1,356 cr is Godrej Capital's cost of funds and Rs839 cr is GIL standalone; Q1FY27 Rs745 cr (Q4FY26 Rs684 cr). Godrej Capital's borrowings grow with its AUM (~35-40% a year), the holding company's debt by ~Rs700 cr a year.
assumptions._taxWhy: The tax line also carries minorities (engine workaround, as in TATACHEM and UPL): GPL 55.23%, GAVL 34.95% and Godrej Capital 8.89% of their profits belong to other shareholders. FY26: tax Rs981 cr + minorities Rs1,171 cr = 63% of PBT (Rs3,393 cr); FY25 58%; Q1FY27 61%. 61% / 60% / 60%.
assumptions._payoutWhy: GIL has paid no dividend since FY20 (Screener dividend payout 0% FY21-26); the cash goes into Godrej Capital.

bull.narrative: Chemicals margins hold near the Q1FY27 level (13%), Godrej Capital keeps growing ~45% a year and the market values it like listed affordable-housing lenders (3x book); the discount stays where it was on 30-Sep-2026 as investors price in listings of Godrej Capital and chemicals.

cover.headline: A basket of Godrej stocks at a discount that has already halved: SELL
cover.lead: Godrej Industries (GIL) is the holding company of the Godrej Industries Group: 23.7% of Godrej Consumer, 44.8% of Godrej Properties, 65.1% of Godrej Agrovet, ~91% of the unlisted lender Godrej Capital, and an oleochemicals business of its own. At 30-Sep-2026 prices its stakes and businesses are worth ~₹1,616 a share after ₹10,157 cr of holding-company debt. The market price (₹1,039) is 36% below that; on the trailing basis we use to track the discount over time it is 32%, against a 61% median since 2021 and 44% since the stock re-rated in 2024. We value GIL the way the street does, as a **sum of the parts less a holding-company discount**, and derive the discount from GIL's own history: **44%**, which gives **{{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}): we initiate with SELL.** The listing plans for Godrej Capital and chemicals are real options, but they are already in the price; the holding company still pays no dividend and borrows ~₹700 cr a year. Bull case {{scen.bull.tp|inr}} (today's discount holds, Godrej Capital at 3x book); bear case {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}.

arguments.h: You are buying three listed stocks, mostly
arguments.p: GCPL, GPL and GAVL are worth ₹50,408 cr (₹1,496 a GIL share) at market, 78% of gross assets. Each can be bought directly, with dividends (GCPL, GAVL) and without a holding company's debt.

arguments.h: The discount has done the work already
arguments.p: GIL traded at a 57-70% discount to its look-through value from 2021 to mid-2024. It is 32% now, after a 57% share-price rise in Apr-Jun 2026 on the group's listing plans while GCPL and GPL fell. Our base (44%) is the median of the post-2024 regime, not a return to the old one.

arguments.h: The holding company is a funding vehicle
arguments.p: Net debt rose from ~₹3,100 cr (Mar-21) to ₹10,157 cr (Jun-26E) to fund Godrej Capital (₹4,283 cr invested) and GPL's equity raises. Interest (₹839 cr in FY26) now exceeds dividends received (₹624 cr). No dividend since FY20; promoters own 74.6%.

arguments.h: Chemicals and Godrej Capital are options, not anchors
arguments.p: Chemicals (₹5,164 cr at 8x Sep-28E EBITDA of ₹646 cr) is a cyclical oleochemicals business with 7-17% PBIT margins. Godrej Capital (₹8,660 cr at 2x book) grows 65% a year at ~6% ROE. Together they are worth ₹13,824 cr, little more than the holding company's ₹10,157 cr of net debt.

catalysts: Q2FY27 results (due by mid-November 2026): chemicals margins after the strong Q1; Godrej Capital funding needs; GPL handovers.

Any outside equity raise or listing step for Godrej Capital: management targets a listing once AUM reaches ₹1 lakh crore and plans ₹5,000-7,000 cr of group investment in unlisted businesses over five years.
New chairperson Pirojsha Godrej (from 14-Aug-2026): capital allocation, dividend policy, any simplification of the structure.

blocks.p: Two things stand out. First, **listed shares are 78% of gross assets**: GIL is mostly a basket of Godrej Consumer, Godrej Properties and Godrej Agrovet, each of which an investor can buy directly. Second, the holding company's debt (₹10,157 cr, ~₹301 a share) uses up most of the value we put on the chemicals business and Godrej Capital together (₹13,824 cr). Buying GIL is buying the three listed stakes at a discount, with a leveraged bet on Godrej Capital and an oleochemicals business attached.

Revenue ₹4,132 cr in FY26 (+22%), volumes +9.4%, exports ₹1,145 cr (28%). Fatty acids (~35% of revenue) and fatty alcohols (~21%) are commodities priced off palm and palm-kernel oil; surfactants (~22%) sell to home and personal care makers; specialty (~11%, volumes +37% in FY26) and biosurfactants are the growth bets. Segment EBITDA was ₹361 cr (8.7% margin) in FY26 and segment assets ₹2,745 cr. Q1FY27 was the best quarter in three years: revenue ₹1,161 cr (+31%), PBIT ₹159 cr (+86%).

sections.title: History: the 2024 family settlement and what GIL ended up with

blocks.p: On 30 April 2024 the Godrej family signed a settlement that split the 127-year-old group in two. The **Godrej Industries Group (GIG)**, controlled by Adi Godrej's family with Nadir Godrej, kept the listed companies: Godrej Industries, Godrej Consumer, Godrej Properties, Godrej Agrovet and Astec LifeSciences. The **Godrej Enterprises Group (GEG)**, under Jamshyd Godrej and Nyrika Holkar, kept unlisted Godrej & Boyce and its affiliates, including the large Vikhroli land bank in Mumbai. Both sides keep using the Godrej brand under a separate brand and non-compete agreement, with no royalty.

sections.title: Oleochemicals: a spread business on imported palm oil

blocks.p: Oleochemicals (fatty acids, fatty alcohols, glycerine) are made by splitting vegetable oils (palm, palm kernel, coconut, rapeseed) and are the renewable alternative to petrochemical alcohols. They go into soaps, detergents and surfactants, personal care, tyres and rubber, lubricants, paints, pharma and food. Prices are cost-plus on feedstock, so revenue swings with palm and palm-kernel oil prices; margins depend on the spread, capacity use and product mix. South-East Asian producers sit next to the plantations; Indian producers import most of their feedstock.

For an Indian producer like GIL three things set profits: (1) the **spread** between product prices and palm, palm-kernel and rapeseed oil (GIL standalone spent ₹3,219 cr on materials against ₹4,105 cr of product sales in FY26, 78%; most feedstock is imported), (2) **capacity use** at its two large plants (Valia, Ambernath), and (3) **mix**: commodity fatty acids and alcohols earn thin, volatile margins; surfactants for multinational soap and detergent makers are steadier; specialty esters, food additives and biosurfactants earn more but are still small.

sections.title: The consolidated P&L is large, lumpy and mostly not GIL's

blocks.p: Godrej Industries' consolidated revenue was ₹22,237 cr in FY26 and profit before minorities ₹2,412 cr. Neither number tells you much about the stock. Revenue is the sum of four very different businesses that GIL controls: its own chemicals (₹4,132 cr), Godrej Agrovet (₹10,233 cr, 65% owned), Godrej Properties (₹5,131 cr, 45% owned) and Godrej Capital plus smaller businesses (₹2,741 cr). Godrej Consumer, GIL's most valuable stake, is not in revenue at all: it is an associate, so only GIL's 23.7% share of its profit (₹445 cr in FY26) appears, inside other income.

blocks.p: Profit is even more distorted. Godrej Properties books revenue only when flats are handed over, years after they are sold, and earns most of its profit as "other income" (interest from joint-venture partners and JV profits: ₹3,256 cr in FY26). Of the ₹2,412 cr profit, minorities (55% of GPL, 35% of GAVL, 9% of Godrej Capital) took ₹1,171 cr; GIL's shareholders got ₹1,241 cr, or ₹36.8 a share.

The questions that matter are (1) what discount the market applies to that portfolio, (2) what the chemicals business and Godrej Capital are worth, and (3) how fast the holding company's own debt is growing. The rest of this report is built around those three.

Every rupee GIL has put into Godrej Capital (₹744 cr in FY26, ₹370 cr more in Q1FY27) and into GPL's equity raises has therefore been borrowed.

blocks.h: What the bears and bulls argue

bullets: **Bear:** The holding company keeps borrowing (net debt Rs3,131 cr in Mar-2021 to Rs9,787 cr in Mar-2026) to fund Godrej Capital and GPL's equity raises; standalone interest (Rs839 cr in FY26) is larger than the dividends GIL receives (Rs624 cr), so chemicals profit is needed just to pay interest.
**Bear:** No dividend since FY20 while promoters raised their stake to 74.64%: minorities depend entirely on the share price closing the discount.
**Bear:** Godrej Capital earns ~6% ROE after five years and Rs4,283 cr of GIL money; its value rests on growth and a future listing.
**Bear:** Consolidated profit is mostly other shareholders' and other businesses' profit: of FY26 PBT of Rs3,393 cr, minorities took Rs1,171 cr.

**Bull:** the April-2026 plan to list Godrej Capital and chemicals gives the discount a path to close, the next generation has taken charge, and the stakes themselves are well below their mid-2024 levels (GCPL −38%, GPL −49% from June 2024).
**Bull:** an outside equity raise in Godrej Capital would both stop the holding company's borrowing and put a market price on its biggest unlisted asset.

blocks.p: GIL is valued as a **sum of the parts (SOTP)**: the listed stakes at market (or at the broker's targets for them), chemicals on a multiple, Godrej Capital on book value, less the holding company's own net debt and less a **holding-company discount** for the fact that GIL's shareholders cannot get at the underlying value (no dividends, no buybacks, control stays with the family). Coverage is thin: ICICI Securities used this method with a 50% discount on the listed stakes, but its last note we found is from August 2024 (target ₹1,090), and no other broker published a target in the two years to 30-Sep-2026. P/E on consolidated EPS is not how the stock is priced: most of that profit belongs to minorities or comes from GPL's lumpy accounting.

Listed stakes are at their NSE closes on 30-Sep-2026 (GCPL ₹850.00, GPL ₹1,628.50, GAVL ₹623.55). Chemicals is on Sep-28E EBITDA (half FY28E, half FY29E), the earnings the market will look at in a year. Godrej Capital is on GIL's share of book. blocks.h: The holding-company discount: derived from GIL's own history

blocks.p: House method: at every quarter-end since June 2021 we compare GIL's market value with its **look-through value** on the same conventions as our SOTP: the three listed stakes at that day's market value (from GIL's own quarterly decks), Godrej Capital at 2.0x GIL's invested cost (cost ≈ GIL's share of book: ₹3,913 cr vs ₹3,960 cr at Mar-26), chemicals at 8x the last reported full-year EBITDA (before FY25, PBIT × 1.2, the FY25-26 ratio), other investments at cost, less holding-company net debt (March figures, straight-line between years). The result over 21 quarter-ends: median **61.2%**, range 31.8-69.0%. Measured against the listed stakes alone the median is 60.5%: chemicals and Godrej Capital roughly offset the holding company's debt.

blocks.p: **Judging the median against today.** On 30-Sep-2026 the discount was 32.4%, half the five-year median. The history has two regimes. Until June 2024 the discount never fell below 57% (GIL kept borrowing, paid nothing, and Godrej Capital was a new cash sink). Since September 2024 it has stayed between 31.8% and 51.3%, with a median of 44.2%: the 2024 settlement settled control, the promoter group bought up to 74.6% (the free float is now ~15%), Godrej Capital was ring-fenced under Godrej Investment, and in April 2026 management promised to list Godrej Capital and chemicals. We think the second regime is the relevant one, so our **base case uses its median, 44%**. The bull case keeps the 30-Sep-2026 level (32%: the market is right to price in the listings); the bear case returns to the five-year median (61%: the listings drift and the holding company keeps borrowing). We do not go lower in the base case because nothing has yet changed the cash reality: no dividend, more debt, and no outside money in Godrej Capital.

segments.name: Chemicals (GIL standalone)
segments._why: Oleochemicals (fatty acids ~35% of revenue, fatty alcohols ~21%, glycerine ~10%), surfactants (~22%) and specialty (~11%). FY26 revenue +22% to Rs4,132 cr on volumes +9.4% and higher palm/kernel-oil-linked prices; Q1FY27 revenue +31% (volume +9%, exports +20%). FY27E +15%: Q1 actual, then single-digit growth as the price base rises from Q2. FY28-29E +10%: volume ~8-9% (Kundaim reactor +30% capacity, Valia specialty plant, Kheda ethoxylation, Goa food-additives business, first biosurfactant due in Q2FY27) with flat prices.
segments._marginWhy: Segment EBITDA (PBIT + segment depreciation): FY25 Rs412 cr (12.2%), FY26 Rs361 cr (8.7%) after weak fractionated fatty acid volumes, costlier feedstock and Q4FY26 PBIT of only Rs40 cr. Q1FY27 PBIT Rs159 cr (13.7% PBIT margin) was the best quarter since FY23. The PBIT margin has swung between 8% and 17% (FY20-26). FY27E 11.5% (Q1 strong, rest of year nearer the FY25-26 average); FY28E 11.5%; FY29E 12% as specialty and surfactants rise in the mix.

segments.name: Godrej Agrovet (100%)
segments._why: Animal feed, vegetable oil (oil palm), crop protection (incl. Astec), dairy (Creamline) and foods. FY26 revenue +9%; Q1FY27 +9% (cattle feed volumes ~+15%). 9% a year. GIL owns 65.1%; the 34.9% minority is deducted in the tax line. Consolidated for the P&L only: in the valuation the stake is at its market price.
segments._marginWhy: FY26 EBITDA margin 8.4%, FY25 8.8%, Q1FY27 8.4% (Q1FY26 10.3%) as crop protection revenue fell. 8.3% / 8.6% / 8.8%.

segments.name: Godrej Properties (100%)
segments._why: Real estate revenue is booked when projects are handed over, so it lags bookings by 3-4 years and is lumpy (Q4FY26 Rs3,458 cr, Q1FY27 Rs506 cr). Bookings were Rs34,171 cr in FY26 (+16%) and Rs8,651 cr in Q1FY27 (+22%); deliveries 12.1 mn sq ft in FY26. Revenue FY27E +25%, FY28E +20%, FY29E +15% as the FY23-25 bookings surge is delivered. GIL owns 44.77%; the 55.23% minority is deducted in the tax line.
segments._marginWhy: GPL's own EBITDA is usually negative (FY26 -8.8%, FY25 -1.5%) because overheads and marketing for a Rs34,000 cr booking business are expensed while revenue is recognised years later; most of its profit arrives as other income (interest from joint-venture partners, JV profits; FY26 Rs3,256 cr). -6% / -2% / +2% as deliveries catch up.

segments.name: Godrej Capital and others (residual)
segments._why: Consolidated revenue less chemicals, GAVL and GPL: mostly Godrej Capital (housing finance and MSME/retail loans; AUM Rs27,867 cr at Mar-26, +65%; FY26 total income Rs2,478 cr), plus hospitality, other businesses and eliminations. Residual revenue grew 40% in FY26 and 75% in Q1FY27 (Rs926 cr). FY27E +40%, FY28E +32%, FY29E +28% as AUM growth slows from 65% towards ~30%.
segments._marginWhy: Residual EBITDA was 48% of residual revenue in FY25 and 54% in FY26: for a lender this is profit before interest (Godrej Capital's interest, ~Rs1,356 cr in FY26, is in consolidated interest) and after credit costs, less GIL's unallocated corporate costs. 52%.

assumptions._unallocLabel: Corporate costs not in any block (inside the residual)
assumptions._unallocWhy: Unallocated corporate costs and eliminations are inside the residual block, which is defined so that the four blocks sum to reported consolidated revenue and EBITDA.
assumptions._capexWhy: Consolidated purchase of fixed assets: FY24 Rs1,197 cr, FY25 Rs781 cr, FY26 Rs1,028 cr (chemicals ~Rs135 cr, the rest mainly GAVL and GPL's commercial assets). Rs1,200-1,300 cr a year.
assumptions._depWhy: FY26 depreciation Rs501 cr = 5.1% of average gross block (Rs9,776 cr); Q1FY27 Rs133 cr (Rs532 cr annualised). 5.2% gives ~Rs560 cr in FY27E.
assumptions._treasuryWhy: Net-debt group (borrowings Rs51,564 cr at Mar-26, most of it Godrej Capital's lending book and GPL's project debt); other income is entered separately.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Screener other income includes the share of profit of associates (mainly 23.7% of Godrej Consumer, Rs445 cr in FY26) and exceptional items: FY25 Rs2,636 cr, FY26 Rs4,123 cr, Q1FY27 Rs1,036 cr (Q1FY26 Rs1,352 cr). Most of it is Godrej Properties' interest income from JV partners and JV profits (GPL other income FY26 Rs3,256 cr, Q1FY27 Rs839 cr). FY27E Rs4,000 cr (Q1 run-rate), then +10% a year with GCPL and GPL.
assumptions._interestLabel: Interest (incl. Godrej Capital's cost of funds)
assumptions._interestWhy: FY26 Rs2,470 cr, of which ~Rs1,356 cr is Godrej Capital's cost of funds and Rs839 cr is GIL standalone; Q1FY27 Rs745 cr (Q4FY26 Rs684 cr). Godrej Capital's borrowings grow with its AUM (~35-40% a year), the holding company's debt by ~Rs700 cr a year.
assumptions._taxWhy: The tax line also carries minorities (engine workaround, as in TATACHEM and UPL): GPL 55.23%, GAVL 34.95% and Godrej Capital 8.89% of their profits belong to other shareholders.
